sentences.text: Leptosuchus is an extinct genus of parasuchid phytosaurs with a complex taxonomic history.
The animal belongs to the parent group Leptosuchomorpha, is classified within the family Parasuchidae, and is classified as a reptile.
Fossils of Leptosuchus have been found in the Dockum Group and lower Chinle Formation in Texas, New Mexico, and Arizona.
The type species L. crosbiensis was named in 1922 based on material found in Texas.
The species L. studeri was named in 1934 based on a skull found in Potter County, Texas.
Recent studies generally classify the species L. adamanensis, L. lithodendrorum, and L. gregorii as belonging to the genus Smilosuchus.
Leptosuchus lived during the Norian stage of the Late Triassic, between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago.
Some paleontologists debate whether Leptosuchus and Machaeroprosopus are synonymous with the genus Rutiodon.
It is debated whether differences between Leptosuchus, Machaeroprosopus, and Rutiodon represent sexual dimorphism, growth stages, or individual variation.
